checks.name: identity
checks.reason: The subject matches the requested plush toy-style panda with black eye patches and black/ivory palette, plus a small green dragon perched on the shoulder; overall toy proportions and key markings align with the provided reference portrait intent (selected-reference vs delivered-portrait; also consistent across native/exported multiviews).

checks.name: appearance
checks.reason: Native render reads as a plush panda with short groomed fur and clean black/ivory boundaries, and the green shoulder dragon remains distinct (native-views). However, the exported representation shows conspicuous portable-coat/card artifacts: patchy/broken silhouette with visible dotting/speckle and sparse tufts across the white areas and along color boundaries, reading less like “neatly groomed short fur” and more like scattered cards (exported-views, motion-00). In the exported peak-stretch pose there is also an obvious visual discontinuity/patch on the torso/side region that reads like coat/skin breakup rather than continuous plush fur (isolated-exported-toy_dance).

checks.name: framing
checks.reason: Full-body panda plus shoulder dragon are visible in front/side/back/three-quarter multiviews for both native and exported, and the motion sheet shows the character sufficiently to evaluate the dance beats and dragon perch; no extra props/scenery are introduced in the reviewed renders.

checks.name: deformation
checks.reason: During the dance, the exported model exhibits a noticeable surface breakup in the greatest-recorded-stretch pose (a large irregular light patch/discontinuity on the side/torso near the moving arm area), indicating problematic deformation/coverage under articulation in the exported representation (isolated-exported-toy_dance). Native looks more stable in the comparable pose, suggesting the issue is export/portable-coat/weighting related rather than purely the authored motion (isolated-native-toy_dance, motion-00).

limitations: Motion evidence is provided as contact sheets and a single isolated peak-stretch pose; this does not prove continuous collision avoidance, ground contact, or seamless looping (evidence-motion-00).
Dragon attachment is assessed visually in sampled frames only; no claim is made about contact forces or interpenetration beyond what is visible (evidence-motion-00).
required_repairs: Fix exported portable-fur/coat continuity and density: reduce visible card speckling/bald patches, especially on white fur areas and along black/white boundaries; ensure the exported look matches the native “short neatly groomed plush fur” (evidence-exported-views, evidence-motion-00).

Resolve the exported deformation/coverage failure visible at peak stretch (side/torso near the arm): adjust skin weights and/or coat masking/attachment so articulation does not expose a discontinuity/patch; re-check the worst-pose frame after repair (evidence-isolated-exported-toy_dance).

state_reviews.reason: The motion reads as a cheerful toy dance with alternating side-to-side beats, visible arm swings, and gentle head tilts, and it returns to a similar starting stance by the end in the sampled frames. The dragon remains perched throughout the shown sequence (motion-00). Note: exported representation has a visible surface breakup at peak stretch which is a visual/deformation failure, but the underlying action intent remains readable.

requirement_reviews.reason: Contact sheet shows repeated left-right body sway/pose reversals across the clip, reading as multiple beats rather than a single lean (motion-00); numeric audit also reports rhythmic reversals (action-audit-toy_dance).
Body shows small whole-body up/down and side-to-side variation over successive beats; the hop amplitude is modest but visible in the sequence (motion-00).
Arms change pose over the beat sequence (forearms/hands shift forward/back and up/down in coordination with the sway), rather than staying static (motion-00).
Head orientation changes gently between frames (tilting with the beat) and returns toward neutral by the end (motion-00).
Dragon stays seated on the panda’s shoulder across the shown frames without separating/flying away; it follows the panda’s motion as a perched companion (motion-00).
End frame in the contact sheet returns to the initial overall stance/centering (no held final lean or displaced finish apparent in sampled views) (motion-00).
Arms return from the swung poses back toward the initial relaxed placement by the end of the clip in the sampled frames (motion-00).
Head tilt reduces and returns close to the starting neutral orientation at the end in the sampled frames (motion-00).

review.summary: Identity, framing, and the intended dance meaning read correctly, with the dragon staying perched. The attempt fails visual quality in the exported representation: portable fur/coat appears patchy/speckled and a clear exported deformation/coverage discontinuity appears at the peak-stretch pose. Verdict requires repair focused on exported coat appearance and the torso/arm deformation area.
